name: Tight Grove, University of New Mexico
species: Ponderosa Pine (Pinus ponderosa) and Rio Grande Cottonwood (Populus deltoides subsp. wislizeni)

location.address: Southwest corner of main campus beside Hodgin Hall, 1889 Central Ave NE, Albuquerque, NM 87131
location.neighbourhood: University of New Mexico / Nob Hill

access: Free. Open campus grounds of the University of New Mexico (state-designated arboretum since 1994, ArbNet Level I; trees on public display per sustainability.unm.edu). No entry fee or hours stated for the grounds.
transport: On Central Ave NE at the university's west edge; ABQ RIDE Central Ave routes stop nearby (not checked against a timetable). Walk of a few minutes from the stop.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the grove of pines and grass around a Lobo sculpture on the southwest corner of main campus. It stands directly beside Hodgin Hall, at Central and University.
story:
The oldest trees on the University of New Mexico campus were carried down from the mountains by its students. Around 1905, President William G. Tight took faculty and students up into the Sandia Mountains, collected ponderosa pines, and planted them in a grove beside the university's first building, Hodgin Hall. The grove now carries his name.

The two sources disagree on the details. A university history page gives 1905 and speaks of ponderosas only. The National Register nomination for Hodgin Hall gives 1908 and says Tight and the student body planted Rio Grande Valley cottonwoods as well as mountain ponderosa. Either way the grove is more than 115 years old, and it was listed on the National Register together with the building it shades.

It has stood at the corner of Central Avenue and University Boulevard while Route 66 ran past on Central and Albuquerque grew from a railroad town into New Mexico's largest city. Whether every tree in it is one of the originals, nobody has said; groves get replanted, and we have not seen a record of which trunks are first-generation.

This is one place to stand rather than one tree. Today Tight Grove is the patch of pines and grass around a Lobo sculpture on the southwest corner of main campus, beside the Pueblo Revival walls of Hodgin Hall. It is open campus ground and free.
